entry.title: Pre-Release Testing • Re: 5.0 pre-release discussion
entry.content:
Yeah, I'm back with WebView2 plugin and the dragging/resize logic. But lets leave resize for later.

Later is fine, since while I did find a way to convert Javascript coordinates to Rainmeter ones, the system is still tricky to implement and not finished yet.

It relies not on a single plain formula to convert stuff (like it would have been ideal if the way such coordinates were determined in Javascript was documented in the first place), but on quickly and temporarily !Moving the skin to be dragged at the 0, 0 coordinates of each monitor when dragging starts (via the new built-in variables in 5.0 and a FOR loop), in order to get the Javascript coordinates of the skin's (and monitor's, given the said movement) top left corner, for usage in the conversion to follow.

I don't like this approach as it involves additional skin moving and redrawing that could and should be avoided if the way to convert coordinates were to be available online, but the result is precise and usable since when it comes to the coordinate part within a single monitor, the way Javascript and Rainmeter see it is identical (they're both logical / virtualized). In other words, only how the 0, 0 points on each monitor maps from Rainmeter to Javascript is needed to have the Javascript to Rainmeter coordinate conversion, besides some additional computation.

I'm on my phone now and can't share the code, but it's still shaky a bit and unfinished, so it would only describe what I said above, instead of doing the whole thing. Obviously, if the monitor arrangement is changed while a skin is dragged via RainmeterAPI's !Move in Javascript, this would fail (since for practical reasons the approach is done only once just before dragging starts), but hey, we're not there yet anyway.

entry.content:
Hey, now that 5.0 seems much more stable, can we take a look at the [!Move] Bang behavior again?

Yeah, I'm back with WebView2 plugin and the dragging/resize logic. But lets leave resize for later. First a little reminder about the issue so we're in sync:

WebView2 can't drag the skin window because it's a different window. To achieve a similar dragging behavior one has to write a script that uses the !Move bang. However, right now, if KeppOnScreen is enabled, when one drags the skin close to the screen bounds it will flicker like crazy (see gif below)

crazyflick.gif

This happens because while the skin refuses to go out of the screen, the move bang is still accepting values out of the limit and will move the skin out of the limit before Rainmeter takes it back inside. Could the [!Move] bang be made to respect the user's KeepOnScreen preference? So if you enter out of bounds coordinates it just moves it automatically to the limit, or to the next screen? In other words, make [!Move] respect the same principles manually dragging a skin follows? This would also include SnapToEdges.

entry.title: Pre-Release Testing • Re: 5.0 pre-release discussion
entry.content:
Why is it troublesome? You can have the Rainmeter 5 portable install use your Rainmeter 4.5 setup (skins, layouts, plugins) by removing Rainmeter.ini in the portable install directory. Then you can easily switch between Rainmeter 4.5 and Rainmeter 5. Doing this should fix the MSIAfterburner plugin error.

Regarding the UsageMonitor error, the skin requests Bits Received/sec, which is indeed not valid and does not exist. The counter name should be Bytes Received/sec. These measures were already broken with Rainmeter 4.5, but that wasn't necessarily visible because it didn't error an error in this situation.

Regarding the RunCommand error, UTF-16 is indeed not valid, but was silently accepted by Rainmeter 4.5. It should be UTF16. This error has no functional effect because UTF16 is the default in case of invalid values.

OK, thank you, I'll be back if'n I find more errors to report.
